title: Infinite, Unexhausted Love
description: Infinite, Unexhausted Love in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 216. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In-fin-ite, un-ex-haust-ed Love! Je-sus and love are one! If still to me thy bow-els move, They are re-strained to none.

lines: If still to me thy bowels move,
What shall I do my God to love?
The length, and breadth, and height to prove
Thy sovereign grace to all extends,
From age to age it never ends;
Throughout the world its breadth is known,
So wide, it never passed by one,
Or it had passed by me.
My trespass was grown up to heaven;
O may I to the utmost prove
Deeper than hell, it plucked me thence;
Jesus's love my heart shall cleanse
Come quickly, gracious Lord, and take
My longing heart vouchsafe to make
Assert thy claim, maintain thy right,
And sink me to perfection's height,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
